title: CAS Formal Substrate Manifest
description: Version tracking and schema inventory for the CAS Formal Substrate (CAS-ADR-008). The manifest records which schemas are present in each version, their status, and their role within the substrate.

organization.description: The formal substrate is organized by component (SAGE, ROOT Harness) with domain-specific configuration files produced by domain instantiation documents. Each component directory contains configuration schemas (JSON Schema), API operation contracts (OpenAPI 3.1.0), and data model schemas (JSON Schema) as appropriate.

structure.sage/: SAGE configuration schemas, Core API OpenAPI specification, and data model schemas. vault_config.schema.json is the root configuration schema; it $ref's to the five sub-schemas.
structure.root_harness/: ROOT Harness configuration schemas, Orchestration API OpenAPI specification, event stream schema, and interrupt contracts.
structure.cas_app_api.openapi.yaml: CAS Application API OpenAPI specification (workflow tools mounted under /app prefix).

schemas.title: SAGE Vault Configuration
schemas.role: Root schema for SAGE vault configuration. A domain instantiation produces a single YAML file that validates against this schema.

schemas.title: SAGE Core API Configuration
schemas.role: Stack-wide configuration for the SAGE Core API process (CAS-ADR-030, CAS-ADR-042, CAS-ADR-043). Loaded once at process startup before any vault is registered; carries resources whose enforcement spans the whole SAGE process (the abstraction provider, its model, and the local provider's optional context-window override and clause (f) opener constraint), the deployment-profile marker that co-binds the adapter-port implementations for one deployment target, the durable-storage binding selector (postgres, the storage port's sole binding), the vault-source-store binding selector (filesystem default, tenant document-store alternative), the Postgres storage-engine connection parameters (non-secret; password from the environment), the optional OAuth resource-server auth binding (absent by default; non-secret issuer/audience coordinates when a deployment authenticates its callers), and the caller-local transfer channel block (the public endpoint base minted recipes embed and the one-time token lifetime; omitted by deployments that never mint recipes). The on-disk file is sage/config.yaml at the repo root.

schemas.title: SAGE Document Types
schemas.role: Defines the doc_type enum for a vault's domain vocabulary. Tier 2 (the vocabulary itself), optional Tier 3 metadata_schema (per-doc_type structured metadata schema for tier3_metadata payloads), and optional unique_keys declaration (tier3_metadata fields whose values must be unique within the doc_type, enforced atomically by the storage substrate per CAS-ADR-031).

schemas.title: SAGE Lifecycle State Machine
schemas.role: Defines lifecycle states and valid transitions. Base set is always present; domains extend it.

schemas.title: SAGE Metadata Extraction Configuration
schemas.role: Defines the two-stage metadata extraction pipeline: filename patterns with code-to-doc_type maps, then content extraction rules.

schemas.title: SAGE Edge Inference Configuration
schemas.role: Defines three-tier edge inference model: tier assignments, inference rules, and staging table behavior.

schemas.title: SAGE Edge Type Registry
schemas.role: Per-vault registry assigning a resolution_policy to every edge type used by the vault. Consulted at edge creation for write-time invariant enforcement and at traversal for chain-scoped resolution. See CAS-ADR-017.

schemas.title: SAGE Core API
schemas.role: OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification for the SAGE Core API. Defines the REST surface for discovery, ingestion, lifecycle management, graph operations, access control, utilities, and the token-gated transfer endpoints (the byte legs of the caller-local transfer channel), plus the transfer recipe schemas the MCP tools return. Consumed by the ROOT Harness Integration Layer, MCP adapter, and CAS Application. Source authority: SAGE Architecture Reference Section 7.

schemas.title: CAS Application API
schemas.role: OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification for the CAS Application backend HTTP surface (mounted at the /app prefix). Defines directory scan and batch-ingest endpoints used by the CAS Application UI. Architecturally distinct from the SAGE Core API; the two specs are validated together by tests/sage/test_openapi_conformance.py and must respect URL-prefix boundaries (sage_core_api owns /sage_vaults/*, cas_app_api owns /app/*).

schemas.title: Decision Log
schemas.role: Schema for SAGE-managed decision logs owned by steward and orchestrator agents. Captures operational judgment not recorded in artifact revision histories: decisions not to act, decisions deferred, and cross-artifact reasoning. Append-only with supersession back-references. See CAS-ADR-012.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Pipeline Configuration
schemas.role: Defines pipeline stages, transitions, gatekeeper bindings, and precondition expressions.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Agent Registration
schemas.role: Defines agent registration records: type, owned artifact, autonomy level, capabilities, policy reference, LLM configuration.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Policy Configuration
schemas.role: Defines behavioral constraints: permitted operations, scope restrictions, and tool-level approval policy.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Workflow Graph
schemas.role: Defines LangGraph workflow definitions: nodes, edges, state dictionary, and interrupt placement.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Orchestration API
schemas.role: OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification for the ROOT Harness Orchestration API. Defines the REST surface for workflow triggering, status monitoring, human-in-the-loop interrupt resolution, agent registration, pipeline status queries, and real-time event streaming. Consumed by the CAS Application, MCP adapter, and CLI. Source authority: ROOT Harness Architecture Reference Section 2.5.

schemas.title: AgentEvent
schemas.role: Schema for typed event records emitted by the ROOT Harness event stream during workflow execution. Seven event categories: workflow lifecycle, node transitions, tool interactions, LLM cycles, interrupt lifecycle, steward governance, and checkpoint operations. Consumed by the CAS Application and MCP clients via subscribe_events. See CAS-ADR-013.

schemas.title: Interrupt Contracts
schemas.role: Schema for human-in-the-loop interrupt descriptors and tool-level approval policies. Defines InterruptDescriptor (runtime data structure for pending interrupts), ApproveRequest (resolution payload for the approve operation), and ApprovalPolicy (per-agent configuration for tool-call approval gating). Two interrupt origins: interrupt nodes (autonomy Level 3) and approval callbacks (Levels 1-2). See ROOT Harness Architecture Reference Sections 2.5, 2.7, 4.4, and 5.2.

revision_history.summary: Split source provenance from stored-copy integrity on Document. sage/sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.12->v0.13: Document gains stored_content_hash (nullable, sha256:<hex> pattern), the SHA-256 of the source bytes as the vault-source store retained them, and source_content_hash's description now states what it had always been read as but did not always hold -- the SHA-256 of the bytes the caller delivered. The two differ only under a binding that rewrites its copy at rest: the document-store binding (CAS-ADR-043) uploads to a document library that restamps Office packages, and because projection reads the retained copy back through the port, the recorded provenance hash described the rewritten copy rather than the caller's file. The rewrite is not reproducible, so every hash-keyed behavior failed for docx/xlsx/pptx on a cloud vault: duplicate detection never fired, re-ingest-if-changed always reported a change, and a caller's hash of its own original never matched. Code (not in this spec): sage/services/ingestion.py hashes the delivered file before retention and records that as source_content_hash, keeping the projection-derived digest as stored_content_hash, so dedup and the supersede identical-content check key on content identity; sage/vault_source_binding.py gains hash_file and the VaultSourceStore port gains planned_source_path (where a binding would home a source, no side effects), which lets the ingestion service skip a retain whose bytes are already recorded at that path -- the identical-content reuse a binding whose stored copy is not byte-identical to its input cannot decide for itself; sage/services/maintenance.py audits the retained copy against stored_content_hash, falling back to source_content_hash so records predating the split still detect corruption; sage/storage/postgres/schema.py adds the column plus an ADDITIVE_COLUMNS 'ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS' statement in ddl_statements, so a vault provisioned before the column gains it on its next open. Policy for pre-split records: a null stored_content_hash means the provenance hash is the as-stored digest and the delivered-byte digest is unrecoverable -- no backfill is possible, and re-delivering the original bytes creates a new document rather than deduplicating, remediable by superseding. Tests: MPI-008/009/010 (provenance equals the delivered hash under either binding, byte-identical re-ingest dedups with no second stored copy, identical bytes under a new name still dedup) with the shared fake Graph client now restamping Office uploads so the divergence is reproduced rather than assumed; VSBB-025/026 and VSB-DS-048/049 (planned_source_path on both bindings); source-file audit coverage for a diverged-but-intact copy, corruption of a diverged copy, and the null-stored-hash fallback; additive-column migration over an already-provisioned schema; the bootstrap idempotency gate widened from CREATE to all DDL; the verbatim-description, YAML<->Pydantic parity, router-conformance, MCP-tool-conformance, typed-alias, seam, and public-posture gates pass.

Bound the facets target of search so the default orientation call stays within a fixed size envelope at any corpus size and tagging density (sage_core_api.openapi.yaml 0.11 -> 0.12). The tags facet is free text, so its vocabulary grows with the corpus; unbounded, a densely tagged vault made the recommended first call against an unfamiliar deployment exceed the calling client's tool-result ceiling. Four co-shipped substrate changes: (1) New DiscoverRequest.facet_fields (array of the new FacetField enum component; minItems 1, nullable) selects a subset of the five facet fields; rows always return in the fixed field order regardless of the order requested, and the storage layer skips unrequested aggregations rather than filtering them post hoc. (2) New DiscoverRequest.facet_value_limit (integer, minimum 1, nullable) caps each row's values to the top entries by count-DESC/value-ASC; null applies the built-in default cap of 50 (DEFAULT_FACET_VALUE_LIMIT in sage/services/retrieval.py). Deliberately no unlimited sentinel: a zero-means-everything misreading would reproduce the unbounded-response failure the cap exists to prevent, so full vocabularies are reached by re-calling with the limit set to the reported true total. (3) FacetHit gains required total_distinct (integer): the field's true distinct-value count computed before the cap, so truncation is detectable exactly as total_distinct exceeding the entry count of values; typed non-nullable so the zero survives exclude_none serialization on empty facets. (4) FacetHit, RetrievalTarget, and the search docstring's Facet enumeration block rewritten so the bounded-response claim holds for the default call shape by construction (vocabulary fields by vocabulary size, tags by the cap). Storage port: GraphStore.query_document_facets gains fields/value_limit keywords and returns FacetFieldCounts (values + total_distinct) per field, via a wrapped per-field GROUP BY subquery whose COUNT(*) OVER () is computed before the outer ORDER BY/LIMIT; storage stays policy-free (None = uncapped, all fields) with the default-cap policy in the retrieval service; the correlated-EXISTS tag-filter composition is preserved by keeping the documents table unaliased inside the subquery. Request validator: the two facet parameters are rejected for non-facets targets via mode_parameter_mismatch rather than silently ignored; unknown facet_fields members fail as typed enum errors surfacing the invalid_parameter envelope on both the MCP and HTTP seams. Gates: YAML_ONLY_FORWARD_DECLARATIONS gains FacetField under the existing StrEnum grouping; the self-documentation facet-block gate now also requires facet_value_limit and total_distinct inside the regex-isolated block. New coverage: storage cap/boundary/subset/filter-composition tests with a tie pinned at the cut line (tests/sage/test_graph_store.py), validator interaction matrix and no-sentinel pin (tests/sage/test_retrieval.py), default-cap-without-opt-in and two-step full-vocabulary reachability at the service layer, MCP parameter-forwarding roundtrip (tests/sage/test_mcp_server.py), envelope parity on both seams (tests/sage/test_validation_envelope_parity.py), HTTP response_model re-validation (tests/sage/test_api_integration.py), and a fixed-size-bound regression on a 240-tag vault whose in-test arithmetic guard proves the uncapped payload necessarily exceeds the bound (tests/app/test_mcp_app_tools.py).

Require Document.lifecycle_status rather than letting a model default shadow the configured ingest landing state. CAS-ADR-047 is the governing decision: lifecycle preconditions derive from vault configuration, and engine literals survive only as the defaults an unset declaration resolves to. A model-level default is not such a literal -- it is reachable with no declaration at all, so any construction path that omitted the field inherited `active` whatever the vault declared, and nothing raised: the document simply came to rest in a declared state that this vault's ingest never produces, which no subsequent precondition flags as wrong. sage/models/schemas.py drops default="active"; DocumentWithContent inherits the change. The removal is not justified as a substrate-conformance fix: sage_core_api.openapi.yaml does list lifecycle_status in Document.required, but per the rationale recorded at tests/sage/test_openapi_conformance.py the two notions of required do not map -- OpenAPI's means the property always appears in the serialized JSON, which a defaulted field satisfies -- so the prior default was not a divergence from the YAML, and the same reading applies to the non-optional field in app/src/api/types.ts. No schema file moves. DocumentSummary.lifecycle_status was already required and is unchanged. tests/sage/test_lifecycle_status_default_guard.py pins the behavioural pair (a model that neither invents a state when none is given nor overrides one that is) and a structural gate holding the no-default property for every non-nullable lifecycle_status field in sage.models.schemas, nullability separating a state a record asserts from a filter whose absence means `any`. The gate does not reach model_construct, which bypasses validation by design where a repair workflow must read values the request-side validators reject.

Close the CAS-ADR-020 clause (f) type-restating opener at decoding time, where the bounded post-generation excision cannot reach. sage/sage_core_config.schema.json bumped v0.10->v0.11: the `abstraction` block gains `opener_constraint` (boolean, default false), selecting whether the local MLX provider constrains decoding against the clause (f) opener; Pydantic StackAbstractionConfig in sage/config.py mirrors the description verbatim (Principle 8). The mechanism is a decoding-time constraint rather than further prompt wording, which CAS-ADR-020 records as measured-unhelpful. sage/adapters/abstraction_utils.py gains the pure automaton (`forbidden_opener_continuations`, `opener_sentence_terminated`) reading the same `_DEICTIC_SUBJECT` / `_CLASSIFYING_VERBS` / `_COMPLEMENT_BREAKERS` / `_DOC_TYPE_EXPANSIONS` registries the detector reads, via a new shared `_type_phrase_candidates`, so the constraint's extent is the detector's by construction; only the final word of a candidate type phrase is forbidden, at positions a licensed complement window admits, and both the fresh-word and mid-word readings are returned so subword pieces are walked rather than prefix-blocked. sage/adapters/abstraction_qwen3.py gains `_build_surface_index` (one vocabulary pass mapping normalized surfaces to token ids, built lazily and cleared in unload alongside the template-overhead cache), `_OpenerConstraint` (an mlx-lm logits_processors callable that watermarks the prompt prefix on its first invocation, decodes only the generated suffix, and latches closed once the opening sentence terminates), and `_suppress_logits`; `_generate_sync` passes `logits_processors=` as a kwarg only when the constraint is enabled and the document carries a doc_type, leaving the prompt byte-identical. A fresh processor per generation preserves the determinism property the abstraction path is tested on. sage/mcp_init.py gains `_reject_opener_constraint_for_non_local`, modelled on the context_window rejection and applied on both the local and cloud bindings: the constraint is a property of a sampling loop a hosted provider does not expose, so clause (f) prevention is local-only while detection and the bounded repair stay provider-neutral -- an asymmetry stated in config rather than discovered later. scripts/benchmark_abstraction.py gains `--opener-constraint {off,on}` as an axis distinct from the prompt-construction arms (it changes what the sampler may select, not what the prompt says; refused against --model stub, which loads no tokenizer) and `--ids-file`, which reads an audit manifest as the corpus so the two arms measure the same documents; BenchmarkResult gains `opener_constraint`, serialized to the raw JSON and rendered on the scorecard. strip_type_restating_opener's docstring is qualified: an unconstrained regeneration still reproduces the same opening, but a constrained one is a correction, so stored text may be reached that way; the excision remains the only remedy for output already stored and for providers with no decoding surface. Tests: tests/sage/test_abstraction_opener_constraint.py (blocked and silent shapes, a parametrized extent test asserting the constraint blocks a surface exactly when the detector would flag it, and registry-growth tests that fail if the constraint carries a copy of either registry rather than reading it); tests/sage/test_abstraction_qwen3_opener_constraint.py (surface index, processor watermark/short-circuit/masking, and the provider wiring including prompt-identity and per-call-processor guards); STK-015..018 in test_stack_abstraction_dispatch.py; benchmark CLI wiring for both new flags. The verbatim-description, public-posture, MCP-tool-conformance, typed-alias, and source-delimitation gates pass with no allowlist additions.

Two engine assumptions that a freshly ingested document is `active` are closed, leaving no schema change. (1) The LifecycleConfig validator gains its first advisory class -- logged in both the strict and lenient modes, rejecting in neither -- for an ingest landing state that no `supersede` transition leaves. Such a document is not supersedable until it is transitioned out, so ingesting with a predecessor and version-chain edge inference both refuse against it; naming that at configuration time beats discovering it later as refused chain edges. It advises rather than rejects because CAS-ADR-047 sanctions a review-style landing state, and refusing one would make unconstructible through the write surfaces exactly what a configuration is entitled to declare. (2) Identifier-mention resolution no longer prefers candidates by an `active` literal. The preferred pool is now `LifecycleConfig.supersession_surviving_states()` -- the declared states a supersession does not leave a document in, the complement of `TransitionTable.landing_states("supersede")`. A vault landing ingest outside the base lifecycle's choice thereby resolves mentions to its fresh documents, and under the base lifecycle a chain with a completed head no longer empties the preference and fall through to whichever version was stamped most recently -- which, because a supersession stamps the predecessor last, was the retired one. The batch-inference and retrieval active-state filters are unchanged, per the carve-out CAS-ADR-047 records. Cross-array invariants of this kind remain loader-owned: `sage/lifecycle.schema.json` stays at 0.3.

Lifecycle-configuration load validation covers every transition endpoint and the dependency-satisfying set, and one renderer serves every config-derived state-set precondition. (1) sage/lifecycle.schema.json 0.2 -> 0.3: from_state and to_state gain identifier patterns -- to_state is always a real state ('(new)' is the ingestion pseudo-state and no transition may land in it), from_state is that or the '(new)' literal -- and the schema description now states which invariants it carries and which the loader owns alone. (2) The LifecycleConfig validator gains two unconditional rules: every transition endpoint must name a declared state (subsuming the former '(new)'-row-only check), because a transition into an undeclared state strands the document with no valid action out; and no lifecycle may resolve to an empty dependency-satisfying set, which would fail every depends_on precondition permanently with nothing naming the configuration as the cause. Both ride the established strictness split -- the vault-create and update-config paths reject, on-disk configurations warn and load so a vault stays reachable for repair. A lifecycle that replaces the base set entirely must now declare satisfies_dependency on at least one state, since it inherits no engine default. (3) A shared render_state_set renders every caller-facing lifecycle state set: sorted, ' or '-joined, with one documented placeholder '(none)' for the empty set. The check_preconditions payload, the supersede_target_not_active error, and the refused-supersede inference warning all render through it, replacing three divergent inline renderings. The error's ['active'] empty-set fallback is removed: a table permitting supersede from no state now reports an empty allowed_states and a required_state of '(none)' rather than naming a state the vault does not permit. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml, the ingestion router description, and the MCP tool docstring state the empty case in lockstep. Tests: tests/sage/test_lifecycle_config_validation.py, tests/sage/test_state_set_rendering.py, tests/sage/test_dependency_satisfaction_config_driven.py.

Two lifecycle preconditions move from code literals into the vault configuration, and the lifecycle schema's inert constraint becomes an enforced contract. (1) sage/lifecycle.schema.json 0.1 -> 0.2: the states/items object gains satisfies_dependency (boolean|null, default null) -- whether documents in the state satisfy inbound depends_on preconditions, with null deferring to the engine default (active and completed satisfy). GraphOps check_preconditions derives its satisfying set and its required-string payload from the declared states instead of a hardcoded frozenset, so a vault can opt a domain state in or a base state out. (2) The transitions array now expresses the structural ingestion-row invariants directly: exactly one '(new)' row (contains with minContains/maxContains 1) whose action is 'ingest', with 'ingest' reserved to that row (item-level conditionals), so a config that would make ingest user-invocable or leave the landing state undefined fails schema validation. The remaining invariants -- the '(new)' row landing in a declared state, and the base_states_required promise (base states declared, each base action used by at least one transition) -- are enforced by a LifecycleConfig model validator. Strictness is contextual: the vault-create and update-config API paths reject a violating configuration (the vault keeps its previous config), while load_vault_config validates on-disk files leniently, logging each problem and loading anyway so an existing vault stays registered and reachable for repair. base_states_required drops its unenforced const:true and both descriptions state the enforced contract. (3) The ingest landing state becomes readable: TransitionTable captures the '(new)' row's target (without making ingest user-invocable) and exposes ingest_landing_state(), which raises rather than guessing when no row was declared; IngestionService lands new documents there instead of hardcoding active. (4) Description corrections in sage_core_api.openapi.yaml with lockstep Pydantic mirrors (Principle 8): IngestRequest.predecessor_id no longer hardcodes the supersede landing state as archived (it names the table-derived landing, archived under the base lifecycle); PreconditionCheck.required documents the derived-from-config contract; the verify_preconditions operation description now states the actual pipeline gate (not failed -- a mid-pipeline target is not rejected) instead of overclaiming a terminal-status requirement; the LifecycleStatus enum description no longer asserts the base set is unconditionally present. MCP tool docstrings for ingest_document, create_edges, and verify_preconditions follow, as do the tests/sage/contract_tests.md minimal-baseline inputs (VC-001/VC-002 declare base_states_required: false, matching what the loader accepts). Tests: tests/sage/test_dependency_satisfaction_config_driven.py, tests/sage/test_ingest_landing_state_table_driven.py, tests/sage/test_lifecycle_config_validation.py.

Caller-side wait guidance replaces per-turn poll guidance on the surfaces that dispatch pipeline stages as a background task. No structural surface change: sage_core_api.openapi.yaml operation descriptions for the ingest, get-document, and recompute-abstract operations, plus the ReabstractStartedResponse.dispatched_at property description, are reworded to direct callers to wait for a terminal pipeline_status -- naming the full terminal set and the unbounded-wait hazard when a process restarts mid-job -- instead of instructing them to poll. The prior wording invited one status request per unit of caller work, which for an agent caller means a turn and a result payload per tick for the duration of the work. Mirrored Pydantic Field descriptions in sage/models/schemas.py move in lockstep (Principle 8, verbatim descriptions), as do the MCP tool docstrings in sage/sage_api_tools.py and the service-layer docstrings in sage/services/ingestion.py. Descriptions of the server's own internal polling (the deferred-abstract sweep, the SSE progress events) and of endpoints that are genuinely inexpensive to poll (vault stats) are deliberately unchanged. Enforced by three docstring invariants in tests/sage/test_mcp_self_documentation.py: the async-dispatch tools must name every member of TERMINAL_PIPELINE_STATUSES, must carry the wait direction rather than the retired poll phrasing, and must stay free of caller-environment specifics. Per-schema versions are unchanged: no field, path, type, or operation moved.

Published-string ticket-reference sweep across the committed substrate. No structural surface change: sage_core_api.openapi.yaml description and summary text, vault_config.schema.json, edge_inference.schema.json, and this manifest's revision-history summaries are reworded to describe behavior instead of citing work-ticket ids (the hyphenated T-NNNN form), retaining CAS-ADR anchors where a citation is load-bearing; the edge_inference placeholder examples now illustrate resolution with ADR-form identifiers. Mirrored Pydantic Field descriptions in sage/models/schemas.py and sage/config.py move in lockstep (Principle 8, verbatim descriptions). Enforced by a new public-posture invariant in tests/test_public_posture.py that gates ticket ids in published strings -- Pydantic Field descriptions, argparse help text, raise and logging message literals, and all tracked YAML/JSON text -- landing with its allowlist empty. Per-schema versions are unchanged: no field, path, type, or operation moved.

Facets target added to the search catalog surface. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.10->v0.11: RetrievalTarget gains the 'facets' member, DiscoverResponse.results gains the FacetHit row type (new component schema), and the discover request/response target, results, and total_available descriptions are updated. search(mode=catalog, target=facets) returns distinct values with counts for doc_type, lifecycle_status, source_type, pipeline_status, and tags, computed within any supplied document filters; response size is bounded by vocabulary sizes, so no pagination parameters apply (non-default limit/offset/sort_by/sort_order/response_mode are rejected via mode_parameter_mismatch).

Maintenance MCP surface renamed sage_admin -> sage_maint (CAS-ADR-034). sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.9->v0.10: the eleven admin_* operationIds are renamed maint_* (maint_recompute_views, maint_list_vaults, maint_create_vault, maint_get_vault_stats, maint_get_vault_config, maint_update_vault_config, maint_verify_vault_drift, maint_verify_vault_source_files, maint_migrate_vault, maint_recompute_deferred_vault_abstracts, maint_optimize_vault_content_store), matching the MCP tool rename admin_* -> maint_* enforced by the test_mcp_tool_conformance operationId-equality gate; REST URL paths (/sage_vaults/{vault_id}/admin/...) are unchanged for wire compatibility. The rename retires the privilege-boundary connotation the admin prefix carried (the surface split is cognitive-load partitioning; authorization is uniform per CAS-ADR-034). Server side (not in this spec): the maintenance mount's canonical path is /mcp_maint with /mcp_admin as a standing alias path, and every admin_* MCP tool name remains callable via a dispatch-level alias mapping (sage/_tool_naming.py MAINT_ALIAS_MAPPING) with no scheduled removal.

Per-vault source-adapter enablement retired (CAS-ADR-046). sage/source_adapters.schema.json is deleted and the `source_adapters` section is removed from vault_config.schema.json's `required` list and `properties`. Adapter availability is process-wide capability fixed by the installed adapter implementations, so the section's `enabled` flag (which gated only directory-scan labeling, producing a scan-versus-ingest asymmetry) and its `file_extensions` key (no consumers; extension mapping is declared on the adapter classes) both go away. The section's live half -- the per-adapter parameter block that supplies the vault-level base for projection settings such as the docx `heading_style_map` -- relocates to a new optional `adapter_defaults` object in vault_config.schema.json, keyed by source type and carrying parameters only. A vault config still carrying the old section loads with it ignored rather than rejected. Downstream: VaultAdapterInfo drops `enabled`, UpdateVaultConfigRequest renames its `source_adapters` field to `adapter_defaults`, and the `adapter_disabled` scan status is retired from ScanResult and cas_app_api.openapi.yaml.

Caller-local transfer channel: bidirectional file movement between a caller's machine and a deployment whose server cannot see the caller's filesystem (CAS-ADR-042 constraint 1 -- the byte plumbing lives below the profile-invariant tool contract). Spec-side changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: two new top-level paths, PUT /upload and GET /download/{transfer_id}, each token-gated by a short-lived one-time direction-scoped transfer token carried in X-Upload-Token / X-Download-Token (the sole credential on these routes; they are exempt from bearer auth at the app and the edge), plus four new component schemas -- UploadRecipe, UploadRecipeItem, DownloadRecipe, TransferUploadResult -- returned by the MCP tools in place of the prior cloud-profile refusals: ingest_document/bulk_ingest_document with an unreachable absolute source mint an upload recipe (one leg per file) and complete via a new MCP-only transfer_token argument; get_document/read_projection with an unreachable write_to_path mint a download recipe promising the exact content_hash/content_size the endpoint will stream. sage_core_config.schema.json gains the transfer block (public_base_url, token_ttl_seconds). The in-request content_base64/filename inline-ingest byte channel and its errors (inline_content_too_large, invalid_inline_content) are retired -- an LLM-mediated caller cannot carry file bytes through its own token stream; the transfer channel replaces it without a size regression. New errors: transfer_token_invalid (410), transfer_not_staged (409), transfer_token_already_used (409), transfer_content_too_large (413), transfer_endpoint_not_configured (500). Add bulk_create_edge, the third sage_bulk_* operation per CAS-ADR-029. New POST /sage_vaults/{vault_id}/edges/bulk endpoint with operationId bulk_link in sage_core_api.openapi.yaml, plus four new component schemas: BulkLinkItem (mirrors LinkRequest field-for-field with `extra: forbid`), BulkLinkRequest (envelope-level items + response_mode + dry_run; per-item dry_run override is forbidden by design), BulkLinkItemResult (echoes source_id / target_id / edge_type for caller correlation, carries status, optional edge body gated by response_mode, created flag, existing_rationale on natural-key hits, and per-item error envelope), and BulkLinkResponse (results + success_count + error_count + total + dry_run echo). Each item is dispatched through GraphOpsService.link_idempotent so the prior natural-key idempotency contract is preserved: a duplicate triple (source_id, target_id, edge_type) returns the existing edge with created=false rather than raising. The batch is NOT atomic (CAS-ADR-029): a per-item SAGEError is wrapped via sage_error_to_envelope and surfaced inside the response while earlier-or-later successful items remain committed. response_mode follows the sibling bulk tools (/): 'light' drops the per-item edge body from success entries; the created and existing_rationale fields are preserved under light because they are the only natural-key idempotency signals; default-resolution rule is >5 items → light. dry_run (/) propagates envelope-level to per-item LinkRequest construction; the per-item edge.id carries the nil-UUID sentinel on the create path or the existing edge id on a natural-key hit. Unlike the document-patch bulk tools, BulkLinkItemResult carries no `changes` block — link is an edge mutation, not a document field patch, so the would-be edge IS the change surface (matching create_edge's single-item precedent). Implementation lands in sage/services/graph_ops.py:bulk_link, sage/sage_api_tools.py:bulk_create_edge (registered through register_sage_tools), sage/mcp_server.py re-export, and sage/api/routers/graph_ops.py:bulk_link (FastAPI route mirroring the OpenAPI path). 44 new tests across three layers mirror the sibling bulk-tool coverage pattern: tests/sage/test_sage_bulk_link.py (26 tests at the MCP-tool surface — MCP round-trip + batch-level validation in Group A, per-item error code parity with create_edge in Group B, idempotency + mixed-batch partial-success in Group C, dry-run sentinel + state-unchanged + error parity + collision-returns-existing-edge in Group D, response_mode light/full/threshold-default in Group E); tests/sage/test_bulk_link_router.py (8 HTTP integration tests via ASGITransport — happy-path 200 + envelope shape, unknown-vault 404, partial-failure still 200, empty items, malformed body 422, response_mode at HTTP layer, dry_run envelope echo); tests/sage/test_bulk_link_service.py (10 service-layer isolation tests against GraphOpsService.bulk_link directly — happy path, partial success on self_referential_edge / unknown document, idempotency, per-item transaction independence, response_mode and threshold defaults, dry_run state-unchanged). Gate tests (test_mcp_tool_conformance.py, test_typed_alias_coverage.py) pass with no new allowlist entries — the implementation is structurally aligned with the OpenAPI spec and uses _VAULT_ID_ADAPTER.validate_python on vault_id. OpenAPI conformance suite (test_openapi_conformance.py) passes; verbatim Pydantic↔YAML description-sync is preserved across the four new schemas.

Unified dry-run mode on seven mutation MCP tools. Adds a `dry_run: bool = False` parameter to the request schemas of `update_metadata`, `bulk_update_metadata`, `update_lifecycle`, `bulk_update_lifecycle`, `create_edge`, and `update_vault_config` (and as a method/query parameter on `delete_edge`, which has no request body). When set, each tool runs every validator in the same order as a real run but skips persistence at the storage call site — no document or edge write, no `metadata_confirmed` flip, no `updated_at` advance, no chunk-store sync, no yaml write, no registry reload. Three new response wrappers and one preview model: `UpdateMetadataResponse` and `LinkResponse` promote the previously-bare `Document` and `Edge` returns so the `dry_run` echo has a home (breaking change on those two single-item paths; bulk-result envelopes, `SetLifecycleResponse`, `UnlinkResponse`, and `UpdateVaultConfigResponse` are extended in place); `VaultConfigPreview` carries the section-level diff returned on `update_vault_config` dry-run. Per-edge non-persistence is marked by the nil-UUID sentinel `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` on would-be `created_edge` (supersede) and would-be `edge.id` (link); the validator on `EdgeIdStr` accepts it because it's a syntactically-valid UUID, and `uuid4` cannot mint it, so a caller that mistakes it for a real id fails loudly on lookup. Three site-specific decisions worth recording: (1) the prior natural-key pre-check is dry-run-only — real-run still relies on the storage uniqueness constraint, preserving the executor-submission bound from the earlier change; on dry-run, the pre-check lifts the gap to the application layer so the no-op outcome is reported faithfully (same shape as the real-run no-op path under `link_idempotent`). (2) `update_vault_config` dry-run NEVER raises `destructive_config_change`; warnings always appear in the response body so the caller can plan a follow-up real-run with `force=true`. `force` is a no-op on dry-run. (3) For supersede, `SetLifecycleResponse.created_edge` is populated on both real-run and dry-run so the field has uniform semantics — the real `id` is non-deterministic at commit time; on dry-run it carries the sentinel. Bulk tools propagate envelope `dry_run` to per-item construction; per-item override is forbidden by design. Documented limitation in the bulk docstrings: each item's dry-run is evaluated against the committed state at batch start, so item N's would-be effects are NOT visible to item N+1 (the field-report scenario: add tag X in item N, try to add the same tag in item N+1 — both report success in dry-run, the second fails on real-run). Internal `link_idempotent` callers (`batch_inference`, `identifier_mention_inference`) keep the existing `(Edge, bool)` tuple return; only the public `link` and the MCP-tool wrapper return `LinkResponse`, minimizing the wrapper-promotion blast radius. New tests at tests/sage/test_update_metadata_dry_run.py, test_set_lifecycle_dry_run.py (incl. supersede), test_link_dry_run.py (incl. the prior natural-key collision), test_unlink_dry_run.py, test_update_vault_config_dry_run.py (incl. destructive-change case), test_bulk_dry_run.py (incl. per-item independence documented limitation). Shared helpers `state_snapshot` and `assert_state_unchanged` at tests/sage/_dry_run_helpers.py provide the universal 'no state was written' proof (snapshot documents + edges + chunk pushdown fields + optional yaml mtime/size; surfaces per-field diff on failure). The OpenAPI conformance suite (test_openapi_conformance.py) passes including the verbatim Pydantic↔YAML description-sync gate; the test_openapi_conformance suite is the parity enforcer for the new schemas and the modified field descriptions on `UnlinkResponse` and `UpdateVaultConfigResponse`.

Unify response_mode across search targets and deprecate response_level (follow-up). Six changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) New DocumentSummaryLight component schema with five properties (id, title, lifecycle_status, doc_type, tier3_metadata) — the stripped shape returned by search when target=documents, mode=catalog, response_mode=light. (2) DiscoverHit.document switched from a single $ref to DocumentSummary to a oneOf<DocumentSummary, DocumentSummaryLight>; full-mode and non-catalog paths still produce DocumentSummary, the new union accommodates the catalog-light stripped variant without weakening the full contract. (3) DiscoverRequest.response_level made nullable with default null (was default 'chunks') and description rewritten to lead with [DEPRECATED] and a worked equivalence map to response_mode. (4) DiscoverRequest.response_mode description rewritten to describe unified cross-target semantics (the previous text scoped the parameter to target=edges only). (5) Validator behavior change in sage/models/schemas.py: the prior branch that rejected response_mode + target=documents is removed; a new branch raises mode_parameter_mismatch when response_mode and response_level are passed together on target=documents (the two now resolve to the same selector via a precedence rule in the retrieval service, so allowing both would let a caller request a conflicting shape). (6) Service-layer wiring in sage/services/retrieval.py: _catalog routes through a new _project_doc_summary helper that returns DocumentSummaryLight for response_mode=light and DocumentSummary otherwise; _results_to_hits resolves include_content from response_mode first, falling back to response_level when only the legacy parameter is set. The >5-results default-to-light threshold rule stays edge-only by design: discover is general-purpose tooling called from every dashboard load; silently flipping the default catalog response shape for existing callers is a backward-compat hazard the threshold rule was never meant to introduce on documents. The asymmetry against the prior bulk endpoints (which DO opt into the threshold default) is in the use case, not the parameter contract: bulk endpoints are batch-by-construction. MCP tool surface: search.response_level signature changed from str='chunks' to str|None=None so callers that omit the parameter don't trip the new mutual-exclusion check when also passing response_mode; the response_mode docstring section is rewritten to carry the four-mode behavior matrix. the prior response_mode rejection test is deleted; new tests at tests/sage/test_retrieval.py cover validator acceptance, mutual exclusion, catalog stripped-vs-full semantics, semantic/keyword light/full equivalence, deterministic ignored, no-threshold-on-documents, and a deprecation-marker guard on the Pydantic Field description. Removal of response_level itself is deferred to a follow-up ticket once external callers have migrated.

Add response_mode parameter to bulk mutation tools (follow-up). (2) BulkMetadataRequest gains the same optional response_mode property on the bulk metadata endpoint. (3) BulkLifecycleItemResult.document description extended to note that the field is absent on success entries when response_mode=light, in addition to its existing absence on error entries. (4) BulkMetadataItemResult.document description extended the same way. (5) ResponseMode component description rewritten to reflect its cross-surface scope (previously phrased as edges-only on search); the per-surface light-mode shape distinction is now explicit. (6) MCP tool surface: bulk_update_lifecycle and bulk_update_metadata both gain response_mode: str|None=None signature parameter and corresponding docstring sections; the parameter forwards into the Request model where Pydantic enforces the enum. Service layer (sage/services/lifecycle.py, sage/services/metadata.py): both bulk methods resolve effective_mode via len(items) > LIGHT_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD when response_mode is unset, then skip populating the per-item document field on success entries when mode is LIGHT; failure entries continue to carry the full structured error envelope regardless of mode. The threshold-default stance for bulk endpoints is deliberately the opposite of the prior decision for search documents: bulk endpoints are batch-by-construction (the >5 case is the surface's primary use case, not an ambient-caller shape change), so the threshold-default automatically engages on the bulk surface where keeps it off the documents-discover surface. Tests at tests/sage/test_sage_bulk_set_lifecycle.py, test_sage_bulk_update_metadata.py, test_bulk_lifecycle_router.py, and test_bulk_metadata_router.py each gain nine cases (T1 explicit light strips document and semantic_abstract; T2 explicit full preserves them; T3 default above threshold returns light; T4 default at-or-below threshold returns full; T5 error envelope intact in light; T6 error envelope intact in full; T7 mixed-result batch in light; T8 invalid response_mode rejected up front with no per-item state change; T9 empty batch with explicit light). The OpenAPI conformance suite (test_openapi_conformance.py) passes for the prior description surface.

Edge inference schema support. Catalog mode and discovery improvements. Document-level response mode and catalog sort parameters. Six additions to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) ResponseLevel enum (chunks, documents) controlling result detail level. (2) DiscoverRequest.response_level property (default 'chunks'); when set to 'documents', suppresses chunk_content but preserves heading_path (best chunk's location) and relevance scores. (3) DiscoverHit.matched_chunk_count (nullable integer): number of chunks from the document that matched the query, useful as a reranking signal. (4) CatalogSortBy enum (title, doc_type, document_date, lifecycle_status) for catalog mode sorting. (5) SortOrder enum (asc, desc). Chain walk endpoint and edge-type breakdown. Three changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) New POST /sage_vaults/{vault_id}/chain endpoint with ChainRequest, ChainResponse, and ChainEntry schemas. Walks an edge chain to both ends from any starting document via recursive CTE, returning an ordered list with head_id, tail_id, query_position, length, and is_linear (fork detection). Designed for version history retrieval on long supersedes chains but works with any edge type. (2) TraversalNode.edge_count (integer) replaced by edge_counts (object, additionalProperties: integer). Per-type edge count map keyed by edge type string. Breaking change from scalar to map. (3) TraversalNode.required updated from [document, edge, depth, edge_count] to [document, edge, depth, edge_counts].

Semantic abstract consumers (CAS-ADR-011). Two changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) DocumentSummary: added semantic_abstract (nullable string) so discover results carry the LLM-generated abstract without a separate get_document call. Enables steward agent orientation and vault-steward discovery as primary consumers. (2) DiscoverRequest: added use_abstract_prefilter (boolean, default true) enabling two-pass abstract-boosted retrieval in semantic and keyword modes. Documents whose abstract matches the query receive a multiplicative score boost; documents without abstracts remain discoverable at natural chunk-relevance scores.

Chain-scoped edge resolution with anchor and retraction primitives (CAS-ADR-017). New schema sage/edge_type_registry.schema.json: per-vault registry assigning a resolution_policy (none / transitive_source / transitive_both / TBD) to every edge type used by the vault; frozen per-edge at creation. Four changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) EdgeType enum extended with instantiated_from (live-tracking derivation, e.g., template instantiation), retracts (meta-edge disclaiming an earlier edge instance), and merged_from (meta-edge recording chain absorption with downstream tombstoning). (2) ResolutionPolicy enum added. (3) Edge schema extended with resolution_policy (required; frozen copy of registry value at creation), source_valid_from_version, target_valid_from_version, valid_until_version, and retracted_edge_id (all nullable); target_id made nullable to accommodate retracts edges. (4) LinkRequest schema extended with the same anchor and retracted_edge_id fields; write-time validation enforces the policy-keyed invariant and produces new 400 error codes EDGE_ANCHOR_POLICY_VIOLATION, RETRACT_TARGET_NOT_EDGE, MERGED_FROM_VALIDATION, TBD_POLICY_EDGE. (5) TraverseRequest: added debug boolean (default false). (6) TraverseResponse: added resolution_path (nullable array). (7) New ResolutionPathEntry schema discriminated by event_type (anchor_hit, anchor_miss, retracts_applied, tombstone_applied). sage/edge_inference.schema.json: edge_type enum extended with the three new values for consistency.

CAS-ADR-017 conformance alignment. (1) ResolutionPolicy enum gains transitive_target value in both sage_core_api.openapi.yaml and sage/edge_type_registry.schema.json, restoring the four-value resolution enumeration mandated by the ADR ({none, transitive_source, transitive_target, transitive_both}; TBD remains as a governance placeholder). transitive_target is the policy-level mirror of transitive_source: target anchor must lie in the queried document's lineage; source endpoint is frozen at derivation with source_valid_from_version null. No built-in edge type maps to this policy today; vaults opting into it via edge_type_registry now have a resolver and validator that honor it. (2) ResolutionPolicy description refined in the OpenAPI spec to document the null-means-not-applicable semantics for transitive_source (target_valid_from_version null) and transitive_target (source_valid_from_version null).

update_metadata patch-mode redesign (CAS-ADR-028 revision). Three changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) UpdateMetadataRequest.tags switched from `array<string>` (wholesale replacement) to `$ref: TagsPatch` (ops object with `add` / `remove`). (2) UpdateMetadataRequest.tier3_metadata added (previously absent in OpenAPI despite being live in the Pydantic model and service layer; pre-existing schema/Pydantic drift closed as side effect), now `$ref: Tier3Patch` (ops object with `set` / `unset`). (3) New `TagsPatch` and `Tier3Patch` component schemas with strict-conflict semantics: adding a tag already present, removing a tag absent, or unsetting a tier3 key absent each return 400 (`tag_add_conflict` / `tag_remove_conflict` / `tier3_unset_conflict`); `tag_patch_overlap` / `tier3_patch_overlap` for disjoint-list violations; `patch_empty` for degenerate empty ops; `legacy_form` raised at the MCP boundary when callers pass the deprecated bare-list / bare-dict shapes, with a worked-example string in the error detail. Conflict errors carry `current_tags` / `current_tier3_keys` in detail (computed inside the document lock, free). `set` on an existing tier3 key overwrites without error (the verb is literal). The merged tier3 dict is validated against the resolved doc_type's metadata_schema after applying the patch in memory; an individually-valid patch that produces an invalid merged result returns 400 tier3_schema_violation. `ingest_document` is unchanged: it still takes `tags` as a list and `tier3_metadata` as a dict (creation supplies complete state). The asymmetry mirrors REST POST vs PATCH idiom and eliminates the read-modify-write ceremony on single-field edits in the cas-ticket-management skill's Workflow 2 and any future skill touching Tier-3-bearing doc_types. Hard break: bare-list / bare-dict forms on `update_metadata` are rejected (`legacy_form` 400); the skill, the CAS Ticket Conventions steering doc, the CAS Failure Record Conventions steering doc, and ADR-028 are revised in lockstep. Pydantic gains `TagsPatch` and `Tier3Patch` models with `model_config={'extra': 'forbid'}` and `model_validator(mode='after')` enforcing the disjoint/non-empty/non-duplicate invariants; `UpdateMetadataRequest` also gains `extra='forbid'` to catch field-name typos. Service layer (`MetadataService.update_metadata`) reads current state inside the existing document lock, applies the patch in memory, validates the merged tier3 against the doc_type's schema, then writes the final field values to the graph store (no storage-layer change; the JSON TEXT columns continue to accept final-value dicts). Coverage at tests/sage/test_request_validators.py (18 new tests on the Pydantic validators), tests/sage/test_tier3_metadata.py (8 rewrites + new patch happy-path / unset-conflict / post-merge / set-overwrite / unset-only coverage), and tests/sage/test_mcp_server.py (8 new tests covering tag-add / tag-remove / combined / conflict envelopes / legacy-form rejection).

Synced-from provenance attributes on edges, schema-only.
